title: Mt.FUJI 100 — VOLUNTEERS (2026 tournament information)
claims: The volunteer page states that its information is for the 2026 tournament and asks readers to wait for updates.
From the 2026 tournament, LINE groups are used by activity for ordinary and emergency communication just before and during the race, and people without their own LINE account cannot apply.
Volunteer shifts are 8 to 10 hours depending on the area and activity, and volunteers may be asked to extend their time depending on the weather on the day.
Some aid stations cannot be reached by public transport and must be reached by car or motorbike: F1 Fujinomiya, F2 Fumoto, F3 Shojiko, F5 Oshino, F7 Nijumagari and F8 Fujiyoshida.
Volunteers travelling to Fuji Hokuroku Park by public transport can use the event loop bus from Fujisan Station or the Fujikyu Highland express bus stop, and a shuttle bus runs from the parking lots.

The volunteer programme includes interpretation roles, mainly English and Chinese; if there are not enough volunteer interpreters, athletes generally contact the interpreter at headquarters or volunteers handle the situation with an interpreter app.

Volunteer recruitment in 2026 ran in two rounds: first-round results were sent on 19 January, second-round recruitment ran from 2 to 13 February with results on 27 February, and manuals were distributed through activity-specific LINE groups on 20 April.

Volunteer tasks include receiving, sorting and returning baggage and drop bags at the Fuji Hokuroku Park gymnasium, including returning drop bags to runners who withdrew from midnight and to finishers afterwards.
